policy: Source material read independently, date-specific claims grounded; lack of journalist/editor signature is NOT hidden; direct-data effects must not be called causal facts. No article reprints.
research_provenance: Public original institutions and statistical releases checked for this internal dossier; this file is curated findings, not downloaded/hash-certified counterpart to GitHub R2_EVIDENCE_PACKETS.json

claims.statement: FOMC 2026-10-28 maintained the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00%; 10 voted for, 2 against.
claims.limitation: Target band is not a realized daily interbank trading rate.

claims.statement: Dissenters Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred a 25-basis-point increase.
claims.limitation: Dissent is not a future path commitment.

claims.statement: September 2026 US CPI was +3.7% year on year, with monthly seasonally adjusted CPI +0.6%, and core CPI +2.6% year on year.
claims.limitation: CPI is not Fed's preferred PCE inflation series.

claims.statement: September 2026 FOMC participant projections projected 2026 total PCE inflation median 3.7% and core PCE median 3.4%.
claims.limitation: Older SEP is not an Oct28 updated projection.

counterevidence.statement: Two participants favoring a hike directly contradicts an inference of unanimous dovishness.
counterevidence.meaning: Policy hold does not identify a consensus about risk.

counterevidence.statement: Elevated September realized CPI constrains an inference that inflation had normalized.
counterevidence.meaning: The Fed's CPI and PCE targets and methodology must be separated.

mechanism.link: Policy vote and statement may affect expected short-rate path; directional effect not calculated in dossier.
Term yields also depend on term premium and fiscal/geopolitical risks; no event-study evidence for Oct28 yield movement.
Corporate/household borrowing costs transmit through funding rates and credit spreads with lags.

falsification: Nov 18 minutes reveal internal decision reasoning
November 10 October CPI can validate or challenge inflation persistence
Daily 2yr/10yr Treasury and OIS responses versus contemporaneous market expectations
remaining_gaps: Oct28 contemporaneous OIS, Treasury, dollar and equity reaction not measured
Claims about market direction and Fed future rate probabilities remain unsupported

claims.statement: NIM Oct28 reports November outlook Consumer Climate at -30.8 points, down 0.2 from previous -30.6 and below -22.5 a year earlier.
claims.limitation: Survey-based forecast indicator, not actual November consumption.

claims.statement: NIM reports economic expectations rose for a sixth month but purchase willingness fell to -11.9.
claims.limitation: Improving macro optimism does not mean consumer spending already rebounded.

claims.statement: Destatis confirmed September CPI +3.3% y/y, energy prices pushed inflation higher.
claims.limitation: Correlation with confidence is not a causal estimate.

claims.statement: Destatis reported August real retail sales +1.3% month on month but -0.4% year on year.
claims.limitation: Monthly and annual metrics have different baselines; retail != total household consumption.

counterevidence.statement: Rising macroeconomic expectations despite worsening purchase willingness means the survey does not support a universal collapse narrative.
counterevidence.meaning: Consumer climate aggregates divergent household channels.

counterevidence.statement: Positive August seasonally adjusted monthly retail growth is a measured counterpoint to weak sentiment, without disproving the forward-looking NIM signal.
counterevidence.meaning: Retail sales precede the October survey and cannot prove November consumption.

mechanism.link: Energy prices may erode perceived real income and major-purchase willingness.
Sentiment measures may precede discretionary consumption; require later retail/private consumption statistics.
Saving intention and actual household saving rate are distinct constructs.

falsification: Subsequent November actual retail sales and private consumption versus October survey
Household real income and employment adjustments
remaining_gaps: October/November actual consumption not available by Oct29
No individual panel data or econometric causal analysis

claims.statement: Bank of Canada on Oct28 raised overnight policy target by 25bp to 2.50%.
claims.limitation: Do not misstate bank rate 2.75 and deposit rate 2.45 as the policy target.

claims.statement: The Bank published 2026 growth estimate 1% and 2027–2028 projections 2% each, conditional on tariffs and energy prices.
claims.limitation: GDP growth numbers are model projections, not observed annual outcomes.

claims.statement: Statistics Canada September all-items CPI was 3.1% y/y and CPI excluding gasoline 2.2% y/y.
claims.limitation: Shows energy contribution, but not that all non-energy items have no pass-through.

claims.statement: BoC governor explicitly discussed arguments for holding versus hiking; holding case cites relatively concentrated energy inflation, policy-hike case cites future pass-through.
claims.limitation: Same-issuer counterargument, not an independent adversarial analyst.

claims.statement: BoC survey-based pass-through chart uses 35 consumer-facing and 190 other businesses, last observation Aug 2026.
claims.limitation: Survey responses and forecast shares are not realized future CPI observations.

counterevidence.statement: Statistics Canada's 2.2% excluding gasoline checks and constrains the Bank's inflation-generalization claim.
counterevidence.meaning: Independent statistics corroborate gasoline concentration, not the inflation forecast.

counterevidence.statement: The Bank's own explicit hold case and excess supply are plausible reasons against immediate further tightening.
counterevidence.meaning: Decision uncertainty cannot be edited out as a one-way hike path.

mechanism.link: Fuel costs immediately raise transport and production inputs.
Businesses may initially absorb costs, later pass through with demand resilience; survey reports expectations only.
Wider CPI persistence could influence policy path; no evidence actual post-Oct decision changes yet.

falsification: Next Statistics Canada CPI composition and monthly seasonally adjusted core measures
Bank company survey expected vs realized price changes
December 9 BoC meeting and further tariff/oil price information
remaining_gaps: Independent model of future energy price pass-through not verified
Numerical probability of additional hikes not estimable from this source set

sources.issuer: U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management

claims.statement: Maurel & Prom Oct22 document page 4 described Kasa-1X discovered gas and estimates approximately 200 billion cubic feet gross, 120 bcf on 60% working-interest basis.
claims.limitation: Volume language does not independently establish SPE-PRMS proved reserves.

claims.statement: Tanzania Ministry Oct28 statement reported 223 billion cubic feet and dates minister announcement to Oct27.
claims.limitation: Different report dates; reserve basis and calculation precision not reconciled.

claims.statement: Absolute difference of the reported gross figures is approximately 23 bcf; not necessarily a change or correction of same underlying reserve estimate.
claims.limitation: Different issuers may use distinct estimate methods or resource classes.

claims.statement: M&P expected possible first production as early as November 2026 with gross potential of 50 mmcfd; this is forward guidance not achieved output.
claims.limitation: No completed production report supports first-flow claim as of cutoff.

claims.statement: BOEM's SPE-PRMS-aligned reserve classification requires discovered, recoverable, commercial and remaining under a defined approved development project.
claims.limitation: BOEM method is background classification, not direct certification of Tanzania project.

counterevidence.statement: Government 223 bcf vs operator approx 200 bcf are separate issuer statements; the difference cannot be resolved without shared interpretation of gross resources and measurement date.
counterevidence.meaning: Not proof either publisher was mistaken.

counterevidence.statement: Resource and reserves technical distinction undercuts conversion of discovery headline into readily bankable, economically recoverable supply.
counterevidence.meaning: Must analyze sanctioned development, recoverability and infrastructure.

mechanism.link: Discovery/proved reservoir must be evaluated through appraisal, recovery fraction and commercial decision before recoverable reserves can be stated.
Field to end-use electricity requires processing capacity, transmission/pipeline and reliable dispatch.
Possible downstream price benefit requires tested additional flow, alternative fuel displacement and tariff mechanism.

falsification: Operator resource classification update and reserve auditor methodology
Actual Kasa well flow/initial production confirmation after Oct29
TPDC/gas transporter/utility capacity and tariff data
remaining_gaps: Whether 200/223 represent same resource class and scope remains unresolved
Commercial production/cost and project financing not verified
